sentences.text: Palaeotriakis was a member of the family Triakidae, a group within the class Chondrichthyes, which includes cartilaginous fish like sharks and rays.
Scientists have found only six recorded fossil occurrences of this ancient shark.
The species Palaeotriakis subserratus serves as the type species, meaning it is the specific fossil used to define the entire genus.
The genus was formally described by Guinot, Underwood, Cappetta, and Ward in 2013.
The genus includes two species that were originally classified as species of Paratriakis.
Palaeotriakis curtirostris was first described by Davis in 1887, while Palaeotriakis subserratus was described by Underwood and Ward in 2008.
Later studies suggest that Palaeotriakis curtirostris actually belongs to the genus Paratriakis rather than Palaeotriakis.
This animal lived between 85.7 and 72.2 million years ago, spanning the Santonian to the Campanian stages.
